title: Reports of Harassment of and Violence Towards Platform Workers
what_it_is: Reports of Harassment of and Violence Towards Platform Workers

sections.label: Police tracking and MOM complaints
sections.summary: Police do not track harassment or violence crimes against platform workers, and MOM has received no such complaints.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Police do not track the number of harassment or violence-related crimes against platform workers per se.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To date, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has not received any complaints from platform workers about harassment or violence.

sections.label: POHA protection and platform ban
sections.summary: Platform workers are protected under POHA, and the platform company banned the customer who displayed violence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Platform workers are already protected through the Protection from Harassment Act, or POHA, where individuals who harass or commit violence against platform workers may be liable for criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, there are already existing laws that actually protect platform workers against any form of harassment when they are conducting their work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We note in this case, that the platform company has also banned the particular customer who has displayed violence against the platform worker from using their platform.

sections.label: POHA penalties and ongoing case
sections.summary: The case is before the Courts and under investigation, and POHA provides criminal sanctions with stiff penalties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I hope he has not sustained severe injuries and that he is recovering well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But this case is still before the Courts and still under investigation, so, I shall not comment further.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under the current law, POHA, there are already criminal sanctions against such offenders and there are quite stiff penalties as well, including, for example, if there are offenders who intentionally cause harassment, alarm or distress, they may be fined up to $5,000 or imprisonment, or up to six months or both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And if there are more serious cases, where the victim is led to believe that unlawful violence will be used, and in this case, violence has been used against him, then the offender could be liable for a fine of up to $5,000 or imprisonment, or up to 12 months or both.

sections.label: Expanding law and workplace control
sections.summary: Expanding the law may not prevent such things, but employers controlling a site can deny or deter people from entering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Expanding the law itself may not prevent such things from happening, but what we can do is to make sure that if the person is working in a particular workplace where employers have control of the site, they can then deny or deter such people from entering the premises.
